rootCauseOneLine: All SQLite reads are synchronous on the single server event loop; the original 11 s thread-list stall (listLatestGoalEventRowsByThreadIds) was fixed by #1204, but the latest timeline page still runs two window-independent whole-thread scans (listTodoSnapshotEventRowsForThread fetching every tool-call payload, and listStoredEventRowsByParentToolCallIds with sequenceBounds=null walking every event with json_extract), reading ~100 MB / 918 major faults for a 1.7 MiB page on a 44k-event thread and blocking every other request for the duration.
proposedFix: 1) Bound the parent/child backfill on the latest page: pass sequenceStart: window.sequenceStart instead of sequenceBounds null in selectStandardTimelineEventRows (apps/server/src/services/threads/timeline.ts ~L1450) and back listStoredEventRowsByParentToolCallIds with a partial index on rows that have a parentToolCallId, so it stops walking all 44k events with json_extract. 2) Make listTodoSnapshotEventRowsForThread index-only: add a partial expression index events(thread_id, sequence) WHERE item_kind='toolCall' AND type IN ('item/started','item/completed') AND json_extract(data,'$.item.tool') IN ('TodoWrite','TaskCreate','TaskUpdate','TaskList','TaskGet') via Drizzle migration, spell the predicate literally and pin with INDEXED BY (verified on the seeded db: plan becomes SEARCH USING INDEX events_todo_snapshot_idx (thread_id=?), 520 rows instead of every tool-call payload) plus a query-plan regression test; or persist the todo snapshot as thread state. 3) Re-measure cold with the profiler; only then consider the shared DB-layer read worker from #1207. 4) Separately lower COMPLETED_EVENT_OUTPUT_TRUNCATION_THRESHOLD_CHARS (32 KB) toward 4-8 KB; the 250 batch is a per-10 s scan limit, not the constraint.
caveats: Absolute stall times were reproduced at ~10x smaller magnitude (0.3-0.46 s cold vs the reporter's 3.4 s) because this host has local NVMe and 16 cores; the transferable evidence is 99.7 MB of disk reads / 918 major page faults for a 1.7 MiB page and the query plans, not milliseconds. I could not throttle IOPS without root. The seeded thread is codex-shaped (70 MB) rather than the reporter's 131 MiB; a claude-code thread with large toolCall results would make the todo scan proportionally worse. That these two scans were exactly what dominated the reporter's 0.37.0 measurement is inferred from the profile shape (medium confidence); the loop-blocking mechanism itself is high confidence. The unit test documents current plans and passes on main (not a failing repro). No screenshots (not a visual bug).
